business_model.basis: Stated in the cited items (P1 Business overview, P4 Company Overview).
business_model.claim: CPI Card Group Inc. is a payments technology company providing physical and digital payment solutions to U.S. financial institutions, processors, fintechs, and prepaid program managers, serving thousands of customers through direct and indirect sales channels.
quotes: CPI is a payments technology company providing a comprehensive range of physical and digital payment solutions for U.S. financial institutions, processors, fintechs, prepaid program managers, and more.
We serve thousands of customers through direct and indirect sales channels and have maintained long-standing relationships with our top customers.

business_model.basis: Stated in the cited items (P1 Overview, P3 Company Overview).
business_model.claim: The company primarily generates revenue by producing and servicing secure debit and credit cards, including Prepaid Debit Cards, issued on the Visa, Mastercard, American Express, and Discover networks.
quotes: Our revenues are primarily generated from the production and related service offerings of secure debit and credit cards that are issued on the networks of the Payment Card Brands, including Prepaid Debit Cards.

We are also a market leader in the production of “Prepaid Debit Cards,” defined as debit cards issued on the networks of the “Payment Card Brands” (Visa, Mastercard®, American Express® and Discover®) but not linked to a traditional bank account, and related secure packaging solutions.

business_model.basis: Stated in the cited item (P1 Debit and Credit Payment and Other Cards).
business_model.claim: Physical card production centers on contactless dual-interface cards using RFID and NFC technology, alongside eco-focused Second Wave and Earthwise cards, metal cards, and non-chip magnetic-stripe cards.
quotes: We primarily produce contactless cards that are issued on the networks of the Payment Card Brands.

Dependent upon design and card construction, our Second Wave® and Earthwise® eco-focused cards incorporate various types and amounts of upcycled material, including recycled ocean-bound plastic (“ROBP”) and recycled PVC.
We also have a variety of metal card offerings that we produce as contact or contactless depending on the needs of our customers.

business_model.basis: Stated in the cited item (P1 Card Data Personalization and Fulfillment; Integrated End-to-End On-Demand Payment Card Solution).
business_model.claim: CPI provides card data preparation, personalization, and mailing fulfillment—expanded into an integrated, on-demand payment card solution through the acquisition of Arroweye—across financial, healthcare, government, payroll, and incentive verticals.
quotes: We offer a variety of data personalization and mailing solutions for both daily and bulk mail programs.
We expanded our card production, data personalization and fulfillment capabilities in May 2025 through our acquisition of Arroweye.

Arroweye’s payment card solutions expanded our customer base across prepaid program managers, payroll related providers, healthcare related providers, and fintechs of all types, in addition to banks and credit unions.

business_model.basis: Stated in the cited items (P1, P4, P6, P10).
business_model.claim: CPI also sells its proprietary SaaS-based Card@Once instant issuance system—servicing approximately 2,500 financial institutions with more than 14,000 active installations—alongside on-premise instant issuance via TRISM and digital wallet push provisioning.
quotes: Our Card@Once solution generates both initial sales revenue for the hardware and recurring revenue from the related card issuance activities.
As of December 31, 2025, we serviced approximately 2,500 financial institutions representing more than 14,000 active Card@Once installations.

Integrated Paytech: primarily provides cloud-based and on-premise solutions that enable customers to issue instantly personalized debit and credit cards at customer locations, as well as other digital payment solutions, including push provisioning for mobile wallets.

business_model.basis: Stated in the cited items (P1 Prepaid Debit Cards and Related Tamper-Evident Secure Packaging Solutions, P4 Segment Overview).
business_model.claim: In its prepaid business, CPI sells open-loop reloadable cards, retail gift cards, Restricted Authorization Network cards, tamper-evident secure packaging, and retail point-of-sale activation data and fulfillment services to U.S. prepaid program managers.
quotes: Our prepaid solutions include open-loop general purpose reloadable cards that are issued on the networks of the Payment Card Brands, retail gift cards that can be utilized for purchases on an open or closed-loop network, and Restricted Authorization Network prepaid cards designed for a unique set of merchants.

For prepaid cards sold through retail, the relationships and processes we developed allow us to provide activation data, including information printed on the packaging which transacts with the retailer’s point of sale system to activate cards for use.

business_model.basis: Stated in the cited items (P3 2026 Changes in Reportable Segments, P4 Segment Overview, P6 Segment Summary Information).
business_model.claim: Beginning in the first quarter of 2026, CPI reorganized its reporting structure from Debit and Credit, Prepaid Debit, and Other into three operating segments—Secure Card Solutions, Prepaid Solutions, and Integrated Paytech—plus Corporate expenses.
quotes: In connection with our increased strategic focus on expanding and developing additional proprietary integrated technological solutions for our customer base and to reflect the manner in which the Company’s Chief Operating Decision Maker (“CODM”), the Chief Executive Officer (“CEO”), manages our business, we implemented a revised segment structure to assess performance and allocate resources, beginning in the first quarter of 2026.

The changes in our segment structure primarily relate to the separation of the results of our proprietary integrated technologically related operations into a separate segment from the former Debit and Credit segment.

business_model.basis: Stated in the cited item (P6 8-K Exhibit 99.1 prose and Segment Summary Information).
business_model.claim: Secure Card Solutions is the largest operating segment, generating $332.6 million in revenue (up 21%) and a 26.1% gross profit margin in the first nine months of 2026.
quotes: Secure Card Solutions segment revenue increased 21% to $332.6 million, driven by increased sales of contactless cards and contributions from the acquisition of Arroweye.

business_model.basis: Stated in the cited item (P6 8-K Exhibit 99.1 prose and Segment Summary Information).
business_model.claim: Prepaid Solutions generated $71.6 million in revenue (up 3%) with a 29.5% gross profit margin in the first nine months of 2026, and a 33.6% gross profit margin in the third quarter of 2026.
quotes: Prepaid Solutions segment revenue increased 3% to $71.6 million, primarily due to increased sales of closed loop prepaid cards, as well as the change in accounting that was implemented in the second quarter of 2025.

business_model.basis: Stated in the cited item (P6 8-K Exhibit 99.1).
business_model.claim: Integrated Paytech is CPI's highest-margin segment, generating $63.0 million in revenue (up 8%) in the first nine months of 2026 with gross profit margins above 55%.
quotes: Integrated Paytech segment revenue increased 8% to $63.0 million compared to strong revenue levels in 2025, primarily driven by contributions from TRISM, while gross profit margins remained consistent at over 55%.

business_model.basis: Stated in the cited item (P2 Risk Factors).
business_model.claim: Revenue is concentrated among key accounts—one customer accounted for approximately 16% of 2025 total revenue and the top 10 direct customers accounted for more than half—under agreements generally lacking exclusivity or medium- or long-term volume commitments.
quotes: The Company had one customer that accounted for approximately 16% of total revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025.
In addition, more than half of our revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025 were from our top 10 direct customers, which include certain Resellers.

Because our contractual arrangements with customers generally do not include exclusivity clauses or commitments to order specified quantities of products on a medium or long-term basis, there is no guarantee that we will receive orders on a consistent basis or on favorable terms, or be able to renew contracts or purchase orders in a given year on favorable terms or at all.

business_model.basis: Stated in the cited item (P1 Overview).
business_model.claim: Long-term revenue demand is driven by continuous payment card reissuance from expiration, re-branding, and replacement, alongside new account openings by legacy issuers and fintechs and consumers switching financial institutions.
quotes: The U.S. payment card solutions market in which we operate has experienced growth in cards-in-circulation over a long-term period, driven by new account openings by legacy issuers and new entrants to the payment card market, such as financial technology companies (“fintechs”) and others.

The U.S. payment card solutions market is characterized by users (primarily U.S. consumers) maintaining multiple payment cards both physically and digitally and by historically stable and recurring revenue driven by the continuous reissuance of debit and credit cards due to card expiration, re-branding, and card replacement activity, and by U.S. consumers switching from one financial institution to another.

business_model.basis: Stated in the cited items (P2, P3, P6).
business_model.claim: Revenue growth and realized pricing also move with contactless mix—contactless cards generally carry higher selling prices than contact-only cards—acquisitions such as Arroweye ($42.8 million, or 7.9% of 2025 revenue) and TRISM, customer inventory practices, and macroeconomic spending.
quotes: Contactless cards have additional technology to process contactless transactions and generally have a higher selling price than contact-only cards.

Revenue increased $62.9 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, primarily due to contributions of $42.8 million, or 7.9% of revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025, from the acquisition of Arroweye as well as increased volumes of contactless cards, partially offset by decreased revenue in our Prepaid Debit segment.
Our business depends heavily on consumer and business spending.
In particular, the rise in the adoption in digital payment systems or mobile payments may make physical cards less attractive as a method of payment.

business_model.basis: Stated in the cited items (P2, P3, P4).
business_model.claim: Cost of goods sold (311,784 (table in thousands) in the first nine months of 2026) is driven by raw materials—notably microchips and antennas, where 93% of 2025 purchase value came from three main suppliers and 74% from one supplier—plus labor, facilities, overhead, depreciation, leases, and shipping.
quotes: Costs include the cost of raw materials, including microchips for all applicable cards and antennas for contactless cards, labor costs, equipment and facilities costs, operation overhead, depreciation and amortization, leases and transport costs.

For the year ended December 31, 2025 approximately 93% of the total value of our purchased microchips and antennas came from three main suppliers, and approximately 74% came from one supplier, including most of our contactless chips.

business_model.basis: Stated in the cited items (P2, P3, P6).
business_model.claim: Inflation and trade tariffs move production and material costs, with gross margin in the first nine months of 2026 aided by approximately $4.0 million of Secure Card Solutions tariff refunds, partially offset by approximately $1.0 million of tariff expenses in other segments and higher depreciation.
quotes: Inflation has adversely affected us by increasing the costs of materials and labor needed to operate our business and could continue to adversely affect us in future periods.
Changes in U.S. and global trade policy and the impact of tariffs have had and may continue to have a material adverse effect on our business and results of operations.

Gross profit margin of 31.4% increased from 31.2% in the prior year period, primarily due to increased revenue and approximately $4.0 million of tariff refunds in our Secure Card Solutions segment, partially offset by approximately $1.0 million of tariff expenses in our other reportable segments and increased depreciation expenses.

Selling, general and administrative expenses increased for the year ended December 31, 2025, primarily due to increased professional service fees and other costs of $6.0 million associated with the acquisition and integration of Arroweye.

These processes are audited for Payment Card Industry (“PCI”) Security Standards Council data security standards compliance annually.

quotes: The Company now expects low-double-digit revenue growth and Free Cash Flow of $50 million to $55 million, up from prior guidance of high-single-digit to low-double-digit revenue growth and $45 million to $50 million of Free Cash Flow.

growth_thesis.claim: To sustain growth, CPI must retain key customers—including one customer representing approximately 16% and top 10 direct customers representing more than half of 2025 revenue—despite contracts generally lacking exclusivity or volume commitments.
quotes: The Company had one customer that accounted for approximately 16% of total revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025.
In addition, more than half of our revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025 were from our top 10 direct customers, which include certain Resellers.

Because our contractual arrangements with customers generally do not include exclusivity clauses or commitments to order specified quantities of products on a medium or long-term basis, there is no guarantee that we will receive orders on a consistent basis or on favorable terms, or be able to renew contracts or purchase orders in a given year on favorable terms or at all.

growth_thesis.claim: Continued growth requires resilient U.S. consumer and business spending and continued reliance on physical payment cards rather than widespread substitution by mobile payments, biometric payments, or direct installment programs.
quotes: Our business depends heavily on consumer and business spending.

Mobile payments, biometric payments and direct installment payment programs allow consumers to make purchases without the need to carry a physical card and could, if widely adopted, reduce the number of debit and credit cards issued to consumers.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in [P6] (Q3 2026 earnings release) and [P3] (10-K Item 7).
growth_thesis.claim: Secure Card Solutions revenue rose 13% to $111.9 million in the third quarter and 21% to $332.6 million in the first nine months of 2026, driven by higher contactless card volumes and Arroweye contributions.
quotes: •Secure Card Solutions segment revenue increased 13% to $111.9 million, driven by increased volumes of contactless cards.
•Secure Card Solutions segment revenue increased 21% to $332.6 million, driven by increased sales of contactless cards and contributions from the acquisition of Arroweye.
Contactless cards have additional technology to process contactless transactions and generally have a higher selling price than contact-only cards.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in [P2] (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors) and [P6] (Q3 2026 earnings release).
growth_thesis.claim: Continued contactless card growth depends on uninterrupted supply from concentrated microchip and antenna vendors—where three suppliers accounted for approximately 93% and one supplier for approximately 74% of 2025 purchased value—and managing tariff costs.
quotes: For the year ended December 31, 2025 approximately 93% of the total value of our purchased microchips and antennas came from three main suppliers, and approximately 74% came from one supplier, including most of our contactless chips.
Changes in U.S. and global trade policy and the impact of tariffs have had and may continue to have a material adverse effect on our business and results of operations.

growth_thesis.claim: Acquisitions have expanded CPI's addressable market and revenue, led by the Arroweye purchase—which contributed $42.8 million, or 7.9% of 2025 revenue—and the TRISM instant issuance acquisition.
quotes: We expanded our card production, data personalization and fulfillment capabilities in May 2025 through our acquisition of Arroweye.

Revenue increased $62.9 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, primarily due to contributions of $42.8 million, or 7.9% of revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025, from the acquisition of Arroweye as well as increased volumes of contactless cards, partially offset by decreased revenue in our Prepaid Debit segment.
With the TRISM acquisition, we believe we have doubled our addressable market in U.S. instant issuance and are now the clear leader.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in [P2] (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors) and [P4] (10-Q Item 2 Cautionary Statement).
growth_thesis.claim: To sustain acquisition-driven growth, CPI must successfully integrate Arroweye and its on-premise instant issuance acquisition and realize anticipated synergies and benefits.
quotes: We may not realize the potential benefits from the acquisition of Arroweye because of difficulties related to integration, the achievement of synergies and other challenges.
Our inability to execute successfully on an acquisition strategy or strategic relationships.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in [P6] (Q3 2026 earnings release) and [P1] (10-K Item 1 Business).
growth_thesis.claim: Integrated Paytech revenue rose 20% to $23.5 million in the third quarter of 2026 at a gross profit margin over 55%, driven by TRISM and Card@Once cloud-based instant issuance growth, with fourth-quarter segment revenue growth expected to more than double.
quotes: •Integrated Paytech segment revenue increased 20% to $23.5 million, primarily due to contributions from the acquisition of TRISM and growth in the cloud-based Card@Once solution, while gross profit margin remained consistent at over 55%.

The Company expects Integrated Paytech revenue growth to more than double in the fourth quarter compared with the third quarter, driven by continued momentum in Card@Once, the contribution from TRISM instant issuance and a more favorable year-over-year comparison.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in [P1] (10-K Item 1 Business) and [P2] (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors).
growth_thesis.claim: Sustaining Integrated Paytech and digital growth requires upfront investment, timely R&D and market acceptance despite limited R&D resources relative to competitors, and strict cybersecurity and PCI compliance.
quotes: Digital solutions often require upfront investment and additional integration but have the potential to deliver incremental revenue and increased margins over time.

We have limited research and development resources compared to many of our competitors, which may result in an immature product development process and lengthy product roll-outs, and competitors may be able to develop and commercialize competing products more quickly and efficiently.

Our failure to comply with the standards of the PCI Security Standards Council and other industry standards, including due to an inability to continue to make investments in our facilities necessary to maintain compliance with such standards.

growth_thesis.claim: Prepaid Solutions revenue grew 15% to $26.9 million in the third quarter of 2026 on higher closed-loop prepaid sales and healthy open-loop package volumes, bringing nine-month 2026 revenue growth to 3% at $71.6 million.
quotes: •Prepaid Solutions segment revenue increased 15% to $26.9 million, primarily due to increased sales of closed loop prepaid payment solutions and healthy volumes of higher-value open loop packages.

•Prepaid Solutions segment revenue increased 3% to $71.6 million, primarily due to increased sales of closed loop prepaid cards, as well as the change in accounting that was implemented in the second quarter of 2025.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in [P2] (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors) and [P10] (Q2 2026 earnings release).

Our indebtedness and the covenants and restrictions in the agreements governing our indebtedness limiting our ability to use our cash flow in certain areas of our business, capitalize on certain business opportunities and pursue our business strategies, all of which could be further impacted if we incur additional debt and could impact our ability to make debt service payments.

material_events.claim: Selling stockholders affiliated with Tricor Pacific Capital Partners sold 2,337,323 common shares plus an exercised underwriters' option for 350,598 shares in a secondary public offering that yielded no proceeds to CPI and concluded Parallel49's ownership position.
quotes: On September 10, 2026, CPI Card Group Inc. (the “Company”) entered into an underwriting agreement (the “Underwriting Agreement”) by and among the Company, Tricor Pacific Capital Partners (Fund IV), Limited Partnership and Tricor Pacific Capital Partners (Fund IV) US, Limited Partnership (the “Selling Stockholders”) and B. Riley Securities, Inc., as representative of the several underwriters named therein (the “Underwriters”), relating to the public offering (the “Offering”) of an aggregate of 2,337,323 shares of common stock of the Company by the Selling Stockholders.

In addition, under the terms of the Underwriting Agreement, the Selling Stockholders granted the Underwriters an option, exercisable for 30 days, to purchase up to an additional 350,598 shares of common stock of the Company.
The Underwriters exercised in full this option to purchase additional shares on September 11, 2026.
The Offering closed on September 14, 2026.
The Company did not sell any securities in the Offering and will not receive any proceeds from the sale of the shares offered by the Selling Stockholders.
•The Company successfully completed a secondary offering of the remaining shares held by Parallel49, fully concluding Parallel49’s ownership position in CPI after nearly 20 years as an investor.

material_events.claim: Donna Abbey Carmignani ceased serving as Controller and Chief Accounting Officer under an agreement with CPI and became eligible for severance payments and benefits.
quotes: Also, on August 26, 2026, the Company announced that the Company and Donna Abbey Carmignani, Controller and Chief Accounting Officer, agreed that she would cease serving as Controller and Chief Accounting Officer effective as of August 20, 2026.

Upon her departure, Ms. Abbey Carmignani became eligible to receive severance payments and benefits under the Company’s existing U.S. Executive Severance and Change in Control Guidelines, which are described in the Company’s 2026 Proxy Statement.

material_events.claim: Brennan Hughes was appointed Chief Accounting Officer with an annual base salary of $350,000, target short-term and long-term incentive opportunities of $200,000 each, a $100,000 restricted stock unit award, and a $150,000 cash sign-on award.
quotes: On August 26, 2026, CPI Card Group Inc. (the “Company”) announced that Brennan Hughes has been appointed as Chief Accounting Officer, effective as of August 24, 2026 (the “Appointment Date”).

In connection with Mr. Hughes’s appointment as the Company’s Chief Accounting Officer, the Compensation Committee of the Board approved the following compensation: (i) annual base salary of $350,000 effective as of the Appointment Date, (ii) target annual short-term incentive opportunity of $200,000, and (iii) target annual long-term incentive opportunity of $200,000.

In addition, the Compensation Committee of the Board approved (i) a one-time restricted stock unit award to Mr. Hughes with a grant date value of $100,000 to be granted on August 31, 2026 that is eligible to vest in equal annual installments over a three-year period beginning on the first anniversary of the grant date, generally subject to Mr. Hughes’s continued service through such date, and (ii) a cash sign-on award of $150,000.

The acquisition was funded through a combination of cash on hand and our available capacity under the ABL Revolver.

material_events.claim: CPI CG Inc. completed a private offering of $285.0 million of 10.000% Senior Notes, entered into an ABL Revolver of up to $75.0 million with JPMorgan, and redeemed the entire $267.9 million principal balance of its 8.625% Senior Secured Notes.
quotes: On July 11, 2024 (the “Closing Date”), we completed a private offering by our wholly-owned subsidiary, CPI CG Inc. (the “Issuer”), of $285.0 million aggregate principal amount of 10.000% Senior Notes due 2029 (the “Senior Notes”) and related guarantees at an issue price of 100%.

Net proceeds from the Senior Notes, together with cash on hand, were used to redeem the entire principal balance of $267.9 million of the 8.625% Senior Secured Notes due 2026 (the “2026 Senior Notes”) as of the Closing Date, and to pay related fees, an early redemption premium of 2.156%, and other expenses.

On the Closing Date, the Company and CPI CG Inc. as borrower (the “Borrower”), entered into a credit agreement with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., as lender, administrative agent and collateral agent (“JPMorgan”), providing for an asset-based, senior secured revolving credit facility (the “ABL Revolver”) of up to $75.0 million.

material_events.claim: CPI, CPI CG Inc., and JPMorgan amended the ABL Revolver credit agreement to increase available borrowing capacity from $75.0 million to $100.0 million.
quotes: On July 2, 2025, the Company, the Borrower, and JPMorgan entered into Amendment No. 1 to Credit Agreement (the “Amendment”), which amends the ABL Revolver to, among other things, increase the available borrowing capacity from $75.0 million to $100.0 million.

material_events.claim: CPI used available ABL Revolver capacity to redeem $20.0 million of its Senior Notes at 103.000% of par plus accrued and unpaid interest.

The redemption was made pursuant to the terms of the indenture governing the Senior Notes, at a redemption price of 103.000% of par plus accrued and unpaid interest to the date of redemption.
